envelope.text: Returns `Result`, where upstream returns `void` and throws: no exceptions

why:
phase-417 stage 3 (2026-09-11) -- CLOSED. The guard landed; what follows is the record of what it was and how it is held.

UPSTREAM'S CONTRACT: `rclcpp::Publisher<M>::publish(const M&)` returns `void` and throws on failure.

THE RETURN TYPE was never the live half and is recorded here so nobody re-derives it: ours is `Result`, RFC-0018 forbids exceptions, so the widening is a constraint and not a preference, and it is LOUD -- `Result` carries `[[nodiscard]]` (`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/result.hpp`, phase-428 W6), so a ported `pub->publish(msg);` warns and the `-D warnings` lanes make that an error.

WHAT WAS LIVE: `publish` was the ONLY entry point on the class with no `initialized_` guard. `publish_raw`, `publish_streamed`, `loan`, `get_topic_name`, `on_liveliness_lost`, `on_offered_deadline_missed` and `assert_liveliness` all had one. On an uninitialised publisher `M::ffi_publish` reached `nros_cpp_publish_raw`, whose only check is `storage.is_null()` (`packages/api/nros-cpp/src/publisher.rs:139`) -- and `storage_` is an in-object array that is never null -- so it reinterpreted zero-initialised bytes as an `RmwPublisher`. Silently wrong, then UB, with no diagnostic at any warning level, reachable straight from `cpp:Node::create_publisher`.

FIX: one line, `if (!initialized_) return Result(ErrorCode::NotInitialized);`, at `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/publisher.hpp`. Disposition ADOPT-BOUNDED rather than ADOPT because the return type still differs for the RFC-0018 reason above; the BEHAVIOUR now matches (upstream also does not publish through a dead publisher, it throws).

THE CLASS, SWEPT, not just the site. Every public entry point in `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/*.hpp` whose body reaches `storage_` without naming `initialized_` was enumerated; `publish` was the only unguarded one. The other six hits are each correct and each for their own reason: `Executor::is_spinning` goes through `cpp_ctx_checked`, which validates the handle and answers false; `Future::is_ready` guards on `slot_ < 0 || !take_fn_`; `Stream::try_next_sized` guards on `!take_fn_`; the other three are constructors and private helpers reached only from an initialised path.

HELD BY: `packages/api/nros-cpp/tests/compile/publisher_publish_guards_initialized.cpp`, a COMPILE+LINK+RUN TU on the `just check cpp` lane. It asserts both halves -- the return code AND that `M::ffi_publish` is never entered -- because a guard that returned the right code after already handing zeroed storage to the runtime would satisfy the first and still be the bug. It re-asserts the six sibling guards in the same run, so a future fix that reaches only one site cannot pass. Negative control, measured against the pre-fix headers: 3 failures, including `publish must not reach M::ffi_publish on an uninitialised publisher`.

issue 1637 (2026-10-05) — ENVELOPE WRITTEN where a porting user reads it: the method's doc comment recorded the `initialized_` guard's history but not the return-type bound; it now states `Result` vs `void`+throw, the `[[nodiscard]]` consequence, and the `NotInitialized` answer.
